import os

import pytest


@pytest.mark.postgres
def test_invoices_table_exists():
    psycopg = pytest.importorskip("psycopg")
    with psycopg.connect(os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://ledgerline:ledgerline@localhost/ledgerline_test")) as conn:
        assert conn.execute("SELECT to_regclass('invoices')").fetchone()[0] == "invoices"

I added `src/db.py` with `get_conn()`, which returns `psycopg.connect(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], prepare_threshold=None)`. I haven't run it or the tests.

I set `prepare_threshold=None` because of a stored project note. In production and staging, connections go through a transaction-mode pooler on port 6432. Server-side prepared statements fail there with "prepared statement does not exist". Local Postgres has no pooler, so that failure would only show up after deploy.

It raises `KeyError` if `DATABASE_URL` is unset. I didn't add a fallback, because `tests/test_db.py` has its own local default and I didn't want to hide a missing deploy config.

Callers should keep transactions short and not hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pool is limited to 20 server connections per service.
